scenes.label: Fourth Planet
scenes.line: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and is also known as the Red Planet for its orange-red appearance. Mars is a desert-like rocky planet with a tenuous atmosphere that is primarily carbon dioxide.

scenes.line: Atmospheric temperature ranges from -153 to 20 °C and cosmic radiation is high across the surface. Mars retains some water in the ground as well as thinly in the atmosphere forming clouds, fog, and frost.

scenes.label: Polar Caps
scenes.line: Larger polar regions consist of permafrost and ice caps with seasonal carbon dioxide snow, but no bodies of liquid surface water exist. Its surface gravity is roughly a third of Earth's or double that of the Moon.

scenes.label: Southern Highlands

scenes.label: Axial Tilt

scenes.label: Noachian Period
scenes.line: During the Martian Noachian period from 4.5 to 3.5 billion years ago, its surface was marked by meteor impacts and valley formation. Erosion, the possible presence of water oceans, and the loss of its magnetosphere also marked the Noachian period.

scenes.label: Hesperian Period

scenes.label: Noachian Surfaces
scenes.line: The Noachian period saw the formation of the oldest extant surfaces of Mars, 4.5 to 3.5 billion years ago. The Tharsis bulge, a volcanic upland, is thought to have formed during this period with extensive flooding by liquid water late in the era.

long_how_voyager_1_became_the_most_dista.title: How Voyager 1 Became the Most Distant Human-Made Object From Earth

scenes.label: Distant Object
scenes.line: Voyager 1 is a space probe launched by NASA on September 5, 1977, as part of the Voyager program. The mission aimed to study the outer Solar System and the interstellar space beyond the Sun's heliosphere.

scenes.label: Communication Network
scenes.line: It communicates through the NASA Deep Space Network to receive routine commands and to transmit data to Earth. Real-time distance and velocity data are provided by NASA and JPL.

scenes.label: Planetary Targets

scenes.label: Titan Priority
scenes.line: Exploration of Titan took priority because it was known to have a substantial atmosphere. Voyager 1 studied the weather, magnetic fields, and rings of the two gas giants.
scenes.image_prompt: A spherical moon surrounded by a thick orange atmospheric haze., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Detailed Moons
scenes.line: It was the first probe to provide detailed images of their moons. The spacecraft's extended mission is to locate and study the regions and boundaries of the outer heliosphere.
scenes.image_prompt: A rocky, cratered moon surface viewed from close range., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Interstellar Crossing
scenes.line: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space on August 25, 2012. This milestone made it the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space.
scenes.image_prompt: A spacecraft passing through a boundary of energetic particles., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Solar Ejections
scenes.line: Two years later, Voyager 1 began experiencing a third wave of coronal mass ejections from the Sun. These ejections continued to at least December 15, 2014.
scenes.image_prompt: Solar flares erupting from the surface of a star., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Thruster Firing
scenes.line: In 2017, the Voyager team successfully fired the spacecraft's trajectory correction maneuver thrusters for the first time since 1980. This firing enabled the mission to be extended by two to three years.

scenes.label: Thruster Revivals
scenes.line: Voyager 1 experienced successful revivals of several thrusters in 2018, 2019, and 2025. As of 2026, two instruments are operational and returning data: the Plasma Wave Subsystem and magnetometer.

scenes.label: Electrical Power
scenes.line: Its radioisotope thermoelectric generators may supply enough electric power to return engineering data until 2036. A 1960s proposal for a Grand Tour to study the outer planets led NASA to begin work during the early 1970s.
scenes.image_prompt: A metal cylinder with cooling fins generating power., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Initial Name
scenes.line: Initially, Voyager 1 was planned as Mariner 11 of the Mariner program. Due to budget cuts, the mission was reduced to a flyby of Jupiter and Saturn.

scenes.line: The mission was renamed the Mariner Jupiter-Saturn probes. The name was changed to Voyager when the probe designs began to differ substantially from Mariner missions.
scenes.image_prompt: An office hallway with vintage space program posters on the wall., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Control System
scenes.line: It has 16 hydrazine thrusters, three-axis stabilization gyroscopes, and referencing instruments. These parts keep the probe's radio antenna pointed toward Earth.

scenes.line: Collectively, these instruments are part of the Attitude and Articulation Control Subsystem, along with redundant units and eight backup thrusters. The spacecraft also included 11 scientific instruments to study celestial objects as it travels through space.

scenes.label: Radio System

scenes.image_prompt: A transmission tower emitting radio waves into the atmosphere., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.image_prompt: A digital timer display glowing in a dark room., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.image_prompt: Metallic containment spheres resting in a protective lead container., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Half-Life Decay
scenes.line: The power output declines over time due to the 87.7-year half-life of the fuel and degradation of the thermocouples. Unlike Voyager's other instruments, the operation of the cameras for visible light is controlled by an imaging parameter table.

scenes.label: Flight Data Subsystem
scenes.line: This table is contained in one of the digital computers, the Flight Data Subsystem. Since the 1990s, most space probes have been equipped with completely autonomous cameras.
scenes.image_prompt: Vintage computer processing units mounted on a circuit rack., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.line: The computer command subsystem controls the cameras and contains fixed computer programs. These programs include command decoding, fault-detection and fault-correction routines, antenna pointing routines, and spacecraft sequencing routines.
scenes.image_prompt: A circuit board with microchips and soldered connections., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Viking Heritage
scenes.line: This computer is an improved version of the one that was used in the 1970s Viking orbiters. The Attitude and Articulation Control Subsystem controls the spacecraft orientation and points the scan platform.
scenes.image_prompt: Vintage mainframe computer hardware with magnetic reels., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Identical Systems
scenes.line: The custom-built AACS systems on both Voyagers are the same. The Voyager 1 probe was launched on September 5, 1977, from Launch Complex 41 at the Cape Canaveral Air Force Station.
scenes.image_prompt: Two identical electronic control boxes sitting on a workbench., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Atmospheric Measurement
scenes.line: Voyager's measurement of the atmosphere's effect on sunlight and Earth-based measurement of its effect on the probe's radio signal were used to determine the atmosphere's composition, density, and pressure. Titan's mass was also measured by observing its effect on the probe's trajectory.
scenes.image_prompt: An antenna dish pointing toward space, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Liquid Hydrocarbons
scenes.line: The thick haze prevented any visual observation of the surface, but the measurement of the atmosphere's composition, temperature, and pressure led to speculation that lakes of liquid hydrocarbons could exist on the surface. Because observations of Titan were considered vital, the trajectory chosen for Voyager 1 was designed around the optimum Titan flyby, which took it below the south pole of Saturn and out of the plane of the ecliptic, ending its planetary science mission.
scenes.image_prompt: A dense orange planetary haze over a dark horizon, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Alternative Trajectory
scenes.line: Had Voyager 1 failed or been unable to observe Titan, Voyager 2's trajectory would have been altered to incorporate the Titan flyby, precluding any visit to Uranus and Neptune. The trajectory Voyager 1 was launched into would not have allowed it to continue on to Uranus and Neptune, but could have been altered to avoid a Titan flyby and travel from Saturn to Pluto, arriving in 1986.
scenes.image_prompt: Diagram lines showing alternative flight paths in space, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Family Portrait
scenes.line: On February 14, 1990, Voyager 1 took the first family portrait of the Solar System as seen from outside, which includes the image of planet Earth known as Pale Blue Dot. Soon afterward, its cameras were deactivated to conserve energy and computer resources for other equipment.
scenes.image_prompt: A solitary speck of light in a vast dark expanse, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Removed Software
scenes.line: The camera software has been removed from the spacecraft, so it would now be complex to get them working again. Earth-side software and computers for reading the images are also no longer available.
scenes.image_prompt: Computer terminal screens displaying streams of code, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Overtaking Pioneer
scenes.line: On February 17, 1998, Voyager 1 reached a distance of 69 AU from the Sun and overtook Pioneer 10 as the most distant spacecraft from Earth. Traveling at about 17 km/s, it has the fastest heliocentric recession speed of any spacecraft.
scenes.image_prompt: A graph showing distance markers in deep space, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Plasma Wave Experiments
scenes.line: Jet Propulsion Laboratory scientists used the plasma wave experiments aboard Voyager 1 and 2 to look for the heliopause, the boundary at which the solar wind transitions into the interstellar medium. As of 2013, the probe was moving with a relative velocity to the Sun of about 61,197 kilometers per hour.
scenes.image_prompt: Laboratory equipment monitoring electronic signal waveforms, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Distance Per Year
scenes.line: With the velocity the probe is currently maintaining, Voyager 1 is traveling about 523 million km per year, or about one light-year per 18,000 years. As of 2026, Voyager 1 is more than 160 astronomical units from the Sun, the most distant human-made object, moving at about 61,000 km/h relative to the Sun.
scenes.image_prompt: Deep space background with distant stars, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Light-Day Distance
scenes.line: Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to reach a distance of one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026. To commemorate the occasion, NASA invited people to Shine Bright for Voyager by shining a light skyward and flashing V-G-R – the three-letter call sign for NASA's Voyager mission, VGR, spelled out in Morse code.
scenes.image_prompt: Sunlight fading into deep space darkness, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Termination Shock
scenes.line: Scientists at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory believe that Voyager 1 entered the termination shock in February 2003. This marks the point where the solar wind slows to subsonic speeds.
scenes.image_prompt: University research building exterior during the day, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Expressed Doubt
scenes.line: Some other scientists expressed doubt and discussed this in the journal Nature of November 6, 2003. The issue would not be resolved until other data became available, since Voyager 1's solar-wind detector ceased functioning in 1990.
scenes.image_prompt: Open scientific journal pages resting on a wooden table, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Inferred Data
scenes.line: This failure meant that termination shock detection would have to be inferred from the data from the other instruments on board. In May 2005, a NASA press release said that the consensus was that Voyager 1 was then in the heliosheath.
scenes.image_prompt: Charts and data printouts spread across a desk, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Ed Stone Presentation
scenes.line: In a scientific session at the American Geophysical Union meeting in New Orleans, Louisiana, on May 25, 2005, Ed Stone presented evidence that the craft crossed the termination shock in late 2004. This event is estimated to have occurred on December 15, 2004, at a distance of 94 AU from the Sun.
scenes.image_prompt: A scientist speaking at a podium before a projection screen, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Amateur Tracking
scenes.line: On March 31, 2006, amateur radio operators from AMSAT in Germany tracked and received radio waves from Voyager 1 using the 20-meter dish at Bochum with a long integration technique. Retrieved data was checked and verified against data from the Deep Space Network station at Madrid, Spain.
scenes.image_prompt: Large satellite dish antenna tilted toward the sky, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Conclusive Evidence
scenes.line: Since June 2010, detection of solar wind had been consistently at zero, providing conclusive evidence of the event. On this date, the spacecraft was approximately 116 AU from the Sun.
scenes.image_prompt: Digital graph showing a flat line at zero, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Test Roll
scenes.line: Voyager 1 was commanded to change its orientation to measure the sideways motion of the solar wind at that location in space in March 2011. After the first roll the spacecraft had no problem in reorienting itself with Alpha Centauri, Voyager 1's guide star, and it resumed sending transmissions back to Earth.
scenes.image_prompt: A mechanical thruster nozzle on a spacecraft hull, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Constellation Ophiuchus
scenes.line: The spacecraft was reported at 12.44° declination and 17.163 hours right ascension, and at an ecliptic latitude of 34.9°, placing it in the constellation Ophiuchus as observed from the Earth on May 21, 2011. On December 1, 2011, it was announced that Voyager 1 had detected the first Lyman-alpha radiation originating from the Milky Way galaxy.
scenes.image_prompt: Stargazing map of the night sky constellations, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Cosmic Purgatory
scenes.line: NASA announced on December 5, 2011, that Voyager 1 had entered a new region referred to as a cosmic purgatory. Within this stagnation region, charged particles streaming from the Sun slow and turn inward, and the Solar System's magnetic field is doubled in strength as interstellar space appears to be applying pressure.
scenes.image_prompt: Swirling cosmic dust clouds illuminated by distant starlight, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Interstellar Electrons
scenes.line: Energetic particles originating in the Solar System decline by nearly half, while the detection of high-energy electrons from outside increases 100-fold. Voyager 1 became the first spacecraft to cross the heliopause in August 2012, then at a distance of 121 AU from the Sun, although this was not confirmed for another year.
scenes.image_prompt: Subatomic particle tracks captured in a detector chamber, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Sunlight Delay
scenes.line: As of September 2012, sunlight took 16.89 hours to reach Voyager 1, which was at a distance of 121 AU. The apparent magnitude of the Sun from the spacecraft was −16.3.
scenes.image_prompt: Sunlight filtering through distant dust clouds, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Supernova Cosmic Rays
scenes.line: In late 2012, researchers reported that particle data from the spacecraft suggested that the probe had passed through the heliopause, revealing a steady rise since May in collisions with high energy particles thought to be cosmic rays emanating from supernova explosions. At the same time, in late August, there was a dramatic drop in collisions with low-energy particles, which are thought to originate from the Sun.
scenes.image_prompt: A bright stellar explosion nebula in deep space, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: High-Intensity Field
scenes.line: On December 3, 2012, Voyager project scientist Ed Stone of the California Institute of Technology said that Voyager had discovered a new region of the heliosphere where the magnetic field was 10 times more intense than Voyager 1 encountered before the termination shock. In March 2013, it was announced that Voyager 1 might have become the first spacecraft to enter interstellar space, having detected a marked change in the plasma environment on August 25, 2012.
scenes.image_prompt: Laboratory instrumentation displaying high voltage readings, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Open Question
scenes.line: However, until September 12, 2013, it was still an open question as to whether the new region was interstellar space or an unknown region of the Solar System. In 2013, Voyager 1 was exiting the Solar System at a speed of about 3.6 AU per year, which is 61,602 km/h.
scenes.image_prompt: A question mark formed by distant star clusters, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Distance in 2016
scenes.line: Voyager 1 reached a distance of 135 AU from the Sun on May 18, 2016. On September 5, 2017, that had increased to about 139.64 AU from the Sun, or just over 19 light-hours.
scenes.image_prompt: A distant probe drifting through the black void of space, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: NASA Website
scenes.line: Its progress can be monitored at NASA's website. On September 12, 2013, NASA confirmed that Voyager 1 had reached the interstellar medium in August 2012 as previously observed.
scenes.image_prompt: A computer browser window displaying a modern space agency homepage, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Anniversary Date
scenes.line: The generally accepted date of arrival is August 25, 2012, approximately 10 days before the 35th anniversary of its launch. By this point, most space scientists had abandoned the hypothesis that a change in magnetic field direction must accompany a crossing of the heliopause; a new model of the heliopause predicted that no such change would be found.
scenes.image_prompt: A calendar page showing late August dates, cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Heliopause Crossing
scenes.line: A key finding that persuaded many scientists that the heliopause had been crossed was an indirect measurement of an 80-fold increase in electron density. The measurement was based on the frequency of plasma oscillations observed beginning on April 9, 2013, triggered by a solar outburst that had occurred in March 2012.
scenes.image_prompt: Deep space visualization with swirling cosmic particles and glowing gases., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Electron Density
scenes.line: Electron density is expected to be two orders of magnitude higher outside the heliopause than within. Weaker sets of oscillations measured in October and November 2012 provided additional data.
scenes.image_prompt: Graph showing scientific data spike against a dark background., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Plasma Spectrometer
scenes.line: An indirect measurement was required because Voyager 1's plasma spectrometer had stopped working in 1980. In September 2013, NASA released recordings of audio transductions of these plasma waves, the first to be measured in interstellar space.
scenes.image_prompt: Vintage electronics equipment on a laboratory workbench., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Solar System Boundary
scenes.line: While Voyager 1 is commonly spoken of as having left the Solar System simultaneously with having left the heliosphere, the two are not the same. The Solar System is usually defined as the vastly larger region of space populated by bodies that orbit the Sun.
scenes.image_prompt: Diagram of the solar system showing planetary orbits., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Sedna Distance
scenes.line: The craft is presently less than one-seventh the distance to the aphelion of Sedna, and it has not yet entered the postulated position of the Oort cloud. In October 2020, astronomers reported a significant unexpected increase in density in the space beyond the Solar System as detected by the Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 space probes.
scenes.image_prompt: Distant icy celestial body drifting in the dark void., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Density Gradient
scenes.line: According to the researchers, this implies that the density gradient is a large-scale feature of the VLISM in the general direction of the heliospheric nose. In May 2021, NASA reported on the continuous measurement, for the first time, of the density of material in interstellar space and, as well, the detection of interstellar sounds for the first time.
scenes.image_prompt: Deep space scientific mapping interface with coordinate grids., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Thruster Firing
scenes.line: In December 2017, NASA fired all four of Voyager 1's trajectory correction maneuver thrusters for the first time since 1980. The TCM thrusters were used in the place of a degraded set of jets to help keep the probe's antenna pointed towards Earth.
scenes.image_prompt: Engineers monitoring telemetry displays in a control room., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Transmission Extension
scenes.line: Using the TCM thrusters allowed Voyager 1 to continue transmitting data to NASA for two to three more years. Due to the diminishing electrical power available, the Voyager team has prioritized which instruments to keep on and which to turn off.
scenes.image_prompt: Computer server racks blinking with activity lights in a data center., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Heaters Turned Off
scenes.line: Heaters and other spacecraft systems have been turned off one by one as part of power management. The fields and particles instruments that are the most likely to send back key data about the heliosphere and interstellar space have been prioritized to keep operating.
scenes.image_prompt: Close-up of industrial mechanical switches on a metal panel., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Operating Expectation
scenes.line: In 2023, engineers expected the spacecraft to continue operating at least one science instrument until around 2025. As of late April 2026, two instruments remain in operation.
scenes.image_prompt: Engineer reviewing technical blueprints at a wooden desk., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Attitude Control
scenes.line: Some thrusters needed to control the attitude of the spacecraft and point its high-gain antenna in the direction of Earth are out of use due to clogging problems in their hydrazine lines. The spacecraft no longer has a backup available for its thruster system and everything onboard is single-string, according to Suzanne Dodd, Voyager project manager at JPL.
scenes.image_prompt: Complex metal piping and valves in an engineering lab., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Software Modification
scenes.line: NASA has accordingly decided to modify the spacecraft's computer software in order to reduce the rate at which the hydrazine lines clog. NASA will first deploy the modified software on Voyager 2, which is less distant from Earth, before deploying it on Voyager 1.
scenes.image_prompt: Computer programming code scrolling down a dark display screen., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Thruster Swap
scenes.line: In September 2024, NASA performed a thruster swap, switching from a clogged set of thrusters to less clogged ones that had not been used since 2018. In May 2025, the team was able to revive the backup thrusters used for roll motion that were unusable since 2004.
scenes.image_prompt: Technician in a clean room adjusting mechanical components., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Telemetric Data
scenes.line: In May 2022, NASA reported that Voyager 1 had begun transmitting mysterious and peculiar telemetric data to the Deep Space Network. It confirmed that the operational status of the craft remained unchanged, but that the issue stemmed from the Attitude Articulation and Control System.
scenes.image_prompt: Radio telescope dish operating under a cloudy sky., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Computer Switch
scenes.line: The problem was eventually traced to the AACS sending its telemetry through a computer that had been non-operational for years, resulting in data corruption. In August 2022, NASA transmitted a command to the AACS to use another computer, which resolved the problem.
scenes.image_prompt: Old mainframe computer components with tangled wiring., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Unreadable Data
scenes.line: Voyager 1 began transmitting unreadable data on November 14, 2023, and its flight data system was unable to use its telemetry modulation unit. Engineers reported in April 2024 that the failure was likely in a memory bank of the Flight Data Subsystem, one of the three onboard computer systems.
scenes.image_prompt: Oscilloscope displaying erratic signal lines., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Repeating Sequence
scenes.line: The FDS was not communicating properly with the TMU, which began transmitting a repeating sequence of ones and zeros indicating a stuck condition. The Voyager team began developing a workaround, and on April 20 communication of health and status was restored by rearranging code away from the defective FDS memory chip.
scenes.image_prompt: Binary code digits glowing on a dark monitor screen., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Memory Limit
scenes.line: Because the memory is corrupt, the code needed to be relocated, but there was no place for an extra 256 bits; the spacecraft's total memory is only 68 kilobytes. To make it work, the engineers deleted unused code, for example the code used to transmit the data from Jupiter.
scenes.image_prompt: Vintage computer memory chip held with tweezers., cinematic space documentary style, highly detailed 8k resolution, dramatic cosmic lighting, photorealistic astronomy imagery

scenes.label: Data Resumed
scenes.line: On May 22, NASA announced that Voyager 1 resumed returning science data from two of its four instruments, with work towards the others ongoing. On June 13, NASA confirmed that the probe returns data from all four instruments.
